```{r}
## Pb overlay intervals from URINE ONLY (2026-11-03). The pooled age/sex models
## above are fit on every matrix, so for Pb they mix blood/RBC lead with urinary
## lead and put the interval an order of magnitude above the urine points the
## panel actually shows. Swap in the same models fit on the urine stratum
## (Coding/Paper1_Submission2/Reviewer_Round2/run_location_unadjusted.sh
##  "Child_Age,Child_Sex,Mat_Age" urine).
.pb_urine <- function(obj) {
  f <- file.path("../../../Output/Dilution_Unadjusted/stageA_urine/Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2",
                 paste0(obj, ".RData"))
  stopifnot(file.exists(f))
  e <- new.env(); load(f, envir = e)
  u <- get(obj, envir = e)
  stopifnot("Pb" %in% names(u))
  u[["Pb"]]
}

## location axis -- the matrix confound (Fig. S15). The old Ba panel had exactly

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## NHANES PAH unit correction (2026-08)
##
## The NHANES extract stores the three urinary PAH metabolites in ng/L while
## every other analyte in the same object is ng/mL. Stored medians are
## NAP1 1810, NAP2 2700, PYR1 71 -- these match the published NHANES ng/L
## reference medians exactly, whereas Ba (1.54), PFOA (4.00), MBZP (12.4) and
## TCP (0.92) are plainly ng/mL.
##
## This stayed invisible for as long as no PAH was plotted: the four analytes
## in Figure 1B were Ba / MBZP / PFOA / TCP. Adding PYR1 exposed it -- the
## NHANES reference row sat 15,500x above every cohort, forcing the panel to
## span four extra decades and overprinting the axis.
##
## After conversion PYR1 reads NHANES 0.071 vs pooled HHEAR 0.00446, ~16x,
## in line with TCP's 33x. The residual gap is the creatinine-correction
## difference (HHEAR values here are corrected, NHANES are not), not units.
##
## Scoped to this figure deliberately: it does not rewrite the shared
## NHANES_Subset_Intervals.RData, which other scripts also read. If that
## extract is ever regenerated, check whether the fix belongs upstream.
## VERIFY against the NHANES codebook (URXP01/URX1NP/URX2NP) before submission.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
NHANES_PAH_NG_PER_L <- c("NAP1", "NAP2", "PYR1")

all_plot_data <- all_plot_data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(plot_value = dplyr::if_else(
    HHEAR_Name %in% NHANES_PAH_NG_PER_L, plot_value / 1000, plot_value))

all_interval_data <- all_interval_data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
    dplyr::any_of(c("Tau25", "Tau50", "Tau75", "Tau95", "Outer_Lower", "Outer_Upper")),
    ~ dplyr::if_else(HHEAR_Name %in% NHANES_PAH_NG_PER_L, .x / 1000, .x)))
```

Create Intervals
--------------
```{r}


expected_taus <- c("Tau05", "Tau25", "Tau50", "Tau75", "Tau95")
tau_name_map <- c(
  "0.05" = "Tau05",
  "0.25" = "Tau25",
  "0.5" = "Tau50",
  "0.50" = "Tau50",
  "0.75" = "Tau75",
  "0.95" = "Tau95",
  "Tau05" = "Tau05",
  "Tau25" = "Tau25",
  "Tau50" = "Tau50",
  "Tau75" = "Tau75",
  "Tau95" = "Tau95"
)

get_quant_object <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NULL)
  if (is.character(x)) return(NULL)
  if (length(x[[1]]) == 0) return(NULL)
  if (is.character(x[[1]])) return(NULL)
  
  x[[1]]
}

get_quant_table <- function(x) {
  q_obj <- get_quant_object(x)
  
  if (is.null(q_obj)) return(NULL)
  if (!"Quantile_Results" %in% names(q_obj)) return(NULL)
  if (length(q_obj[["Quantile_Results"]]) < 2) return(NULL)
  
  q_obj[["Quantile_Results"]][[2]]
}

safe_interval_width <- function(upper, lower) {
  ifelse(!is.na(upper) & !is.na(lower), upper - lower, NA_real_)
}

cap_with_na <- function(x, cap) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), NA_real_, pmin(x, cap))
}

calc_weighted_taus <- function(quant_table) {
  
  out <- c(
    Tau05 = NA_real_,
    Tau25 = NA_real_,
    Tau50 = NA_real_,
    Tau75 = NA_real_,
    Tau95 = NA_real_
  )
  
  if (is.null(quant_table)) return(out)
  
  Tau_Data <- as.data.frame(quant_table)
  if (ncol(Tau_Data) == 0) return(out)
  
  if (is.null(names(Tau_Data))) {
    if (ncol(Tau_Data) == 4) {
      names(Tau_Data) <- c("Tau25", "Tau50", "Tau75", "Tau95")
    } else if (ncol(Tau_Data) == 5) {
      names(Tau_Data) <- expected_taus
    } else {
      names(Tau_Data) <- paste0("V", seq_len(ncol(Tau_Data)))
    }
  }
  
  mapped_names <- unname(tau_name_map[names(Tau_Data)])
  valid_cols <- !is.na(mapped_names)
  Tau_Data <- Tau_Data[, valid_cols, drop = FALSE]
  
  if (ncol(Tau_Data) == 0) return(out)
  
  names(Tau_Data) <- mapped_names[valid_cols]
  Tau_Data <- Tau_Data[, !duplicated(names(Tau_Data)), drop = FALSE]
  
  for (tau in intersect(names(out), names(Tau_Data))) {
    
    curr_values <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Tau_Data[[tau]]))
    curr_values <- curr_values[!is.na(curr_values)]
    
    if (length(curr_values) > 0) {
      out[tau] <- mean(curr_values)
    }
  }
  
  out
}
shared_outcomes <- intersect(
  names(Child_Child_Age_Quantile_Results),
  names(Child_Child_Sex_Quantile_Results)
)

Final_Intervals <- list()

for (outcome_name in shared_outcomes) {
  
  Quant_Age <- get_quant_table(
    Child_Child_Age_Quantile_Results[[outcome_name]]
  )
  
  Quant_Sex <- get_quant_table(
    Child_Child_Sex_Quantile_Results[[outcome_name]]
  )
  
  Curr_Quant <- list(
    Child_Age = Quant_Age,
    Child_Sex = Quant_Sex
  )
  
  All_Weighted_Averages <- list()
  
  for (i in seq_along(Curr_Quant)) {
    
  weighted_averages <- calc_weighted_taus(Curr_Quant[[i]])
    
    if (is.null(weighted_averages)) next
    
    All_Weighted_Averages[[names(Curr_Quant)[i]]] <- weighted_averages
  }
  
  if (length(All_Weighted_Averages) == 0) next
  
  W_Avg_Df <- bind_rows(All_Weighted_Averages)
  
  column_means <- W_Avg_Df %>%
    summarise(across(
      all_of(expected_taus),
      ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )) %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        all_of(expected_taus),
        ~ ifelse(is.nan(.x), NA_real_, .x)
      ),
      Outcome = outcome_name
    ) %>%
    select(Outcome, everything())
  
  Final_Intervals[[outcome_name]] <- column_means
}

Final_Intervals_Df <- bind_rows(Final_Intervals)
```

```{r}
Final_Intervals_Df_Adjusted <- bind_rows(Final_Intervals) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3))) %>% 
  mutate(
    IQR = safe_interval_width(Tau75, Tau25),
    Max_Min = safe_interval_width(Tau95, Tau05),
    Has_IQR = !is.na(Tau25) & !is.na(Tau75),
    Has_Outer = !is.na(Tau05) & !is.na(Tau95),
    Has_Median = !is.na(Tau50)
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
      IQR_unadj = IQR,
      IQR = cap_with_na(IQR, 20),
      Max_Min_unadj = Max_Min,
      Max_Min = cap_with_na(Max_Min, 50),
      Flag = as.factor(ifelse(!is.na(IQR_unadj) & IQR_unadj >= 20, 1, 0))
    ) %>% 
    mutate(Max_Min_Log = log10(Max_Min + 1),
           IQR_Log = log10(IQR+ 1))
```

```{r}
std_study <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_remove(x, '[_]\\w+|:')  # CHECK: ensure this collapse is intended
}

# UNIT CONVERSION (2026-08-11, CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md section 1.1).
# The local to_ng_per_mL() removed here ended in `TRUE ~ value`, so mg/dL,
# ug/mL, ng/g, pmol/mL, nM and kg/m3 fell through UNCONVERTED and were treated
# as ng/mL -- 39,475 rows (5.9%), wrong by factors of 10^3 to 10^6.
local({
  cands <- c("../harmonization_helpers.R", "harmonization_helpers.R",
             "Coding/Paper1_Submission2/harmonization_helpers.R")
  hit <- cands[file.exists(cands)]
  if (length(hit) == 0) stop("Cannot locate harmonization_helpers.R")
  source(hit[[1]], local = FALSE)
})
Child_Data_Targeted <- Targeted_Data_All %>%
  filter(!is.na(Child_PID)) %>%                           # keep child samples
  mutate(
    Units = if_else(is.na(Units), "ng/mL", Units),        # default units
    Concentration = to_ng_per_mL(Concentration, Units)    # normalize units
  ) %>%
  select(-Mat_PID) %>%                                    # not needed for child
  filter(!is.na(Analyte_Code)) %>%                        # require analyte code
  group_by(Study, Child_PID, Analyte_Code) %>%            # average replicates
  summarise(Concentration = mean(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

child_analytes <- sort(unique(Child_Data_Targeted$Analyte_Code))  # vector of analytes

# Build a list of per-analyte wide data.frames keyed by Child_PID ---------
child_list_Targeted <- purrr::map(
  child_analytes,
  ~ Child_Data_Targeted %>%
    filter(Analyte_Code == .x) %>%                         # one analyte
    mutate(Study = std_study(Study)) %>%                   # standardize label
    select(Study, Child_PID, Analyte_Code, Concentration) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Analyte_Code, values_from = Concentration) %>%
    select(Child_PID, Study, all_of(.x))                   # only current analyte col
) %>%
  rlang::set_names(child_analytes)

# MATERNAL targeted data: long -> wide per-analyte list -------------------
Mat_Data_Targeted <- Targeted_Data_All %>%
  filter(!is.na(Mat_PID)) %>%                              # keep maternal samples
  select(-Child_PID) %>%
  mutate(
    Units = if_else(is.na(Units), "ng/mL", Units),
    Concentration = to_ng_per_mL(Concentration, Units)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Analyte_Code)) %>%
  group_by(Study, Mat_PID, Analyte_Code) %>%
  summarise(Concentration = mean(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ replace(., is.infinite(.), NA_real_)))  

mat_analytes <- sort(unique(Mat_Data_Targeted$Analyte_Code))

mat_list_Targeted <- purrr::map(
  mat_analytes,
  ~ Mat_Data_Targeted %>%
    filter(Analyte_Code == .x) %>%
    mutate(Study = std_study(Study)) %>%
    select(Study, Mat_PID, Analyte_Code, Concentration) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Analyte_Code, values_from = Concentration) %>%
    select(Mat_PID, Study, all_of(.x))
) %>%
  rlang::set_names(mat_analytes)
save(mat_list_Targeted, file = "../../../HHEAR_Man1_App/mat_list_Targeted.RData")
save(child_list_Targeted, file = "../../../HHEAR_Man1_App/child_list_Targeted.RData")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Compute means per location (what you already did)
loc_means <- Location_Plotdata_Child %>%
  group_by(Location, curr_analyte) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_value = median(plot_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Function: percentile of one location's mean in another's distribution
mean_percentile <- function(data, analyte, ref_location, target_location) {

  ref_dist <- data %>%
    filter(curr_analyte == analyte,
           Location == ref_location) %>%
    pull(plot_value)

  target_mean <- loc_means %>%
    filter(curr_analyte == analyte,
           Location == target_location) %>%
    pull(mean_value)

  tibble(
    analyte = analyte,
    reference_location = ref_location,
    target_location = target_location,
    target_mean = target_mean,
    percentile_in_reference =
      mean(ref_dist <= target_mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}
```

```{r}

legend_breaks <- legend_df$Location
legend_labels <- setNames(legend_df$pretty, legend_df$Location)


## label_log1p: back-transform log1p break positions to original concentration.
## Dropped scale_cut = cut_si(""), which applies SI magnitude prefixes to a
## ng/mL axis -- it renders sub-1 values as "m" (milli) and so labels a
## concentration of 0.5 ng/mL as "500m". Harmless while every panel topped 1
## ng/mL, but the free x scales below let panels reach into that range.
label_log1p <- function(breaks) {
  trimws(formatC(expm1(breaks), format = "fg", digits = 3, big.mark = ","))
}

# Breaks are computed per panel rather than fixed at 0:7, because the x scale
# is free (see facet_wrap below). Integer steps on the log1p scale, but the
# step widens once a panel spans enough decades to need more than ~6 labels --
# at five facet columns there is not room for eleven, and they overprint.
log1p_breaks <- function(lims) {
  top  <- ceiling(max(lims, na.rm = TRUE))
  step <- if (top <= 6) 1 else ceiling(top / 6)
  seq(0, top, by = step)
}

    data = Location_Plotdata,
    aes(x = log1p(plot_value), y = Location, color = Location, size = NHANES_Flag),
    width = 0, height = 0.15,alpha = 0.35
  ) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c("0" = 0.75, "1" = 2.2)) +

  # 50% point
  geom_point(
    data = Location_interval_points,
    aes(y = n_unique_locations, x = log1p(Tau50)),
    color = "#1A5354", size = 2.6
  ) +

  # 25–75% interval (thick)
  geom_errorbarh(
    data = Location_interval_iqr,
    aes(y = n_unique_locations, xmin = log1p(Tau25), xmax = log1p(Tau75)),
    height = Location_interval_iqr$level_height,
    color = "#1A5354", linewidth = 1.4, alpha = 0.95
  ) +

  # 5–95% interval (thin)
  geom_errorbarh(
    data = Location_interval_outer,
    aes(y = n_unique_locations, xmin = log1p(Outer_Lower), xmax = log1p(Tau95)),
    height = Location_interval_outer$level_height / 2,
    color = "#1A5354", linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.55
  ) +

  # geom_point(
  #   data = Location_LOD_Data,
  #   aes(
  #     x = log1p(LOD_value),
  #     y = Location,
  #     shape = "Study median LOD"
  #   ),
  #   inherit.aes = FALSE,
  #   color = "#111111",
  #   fill = "white",
  #   stroke = 0.8,
  #   size = 2.2,
  #   position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.12, seed = 123)
  # ) +

  #left-side location labels next to each interval
  # geom_text(
  #   data = Location_Plotdata,
  #   aes(y = n_unique_locations, x = 0 - 0.05, label = Location),
  #   hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", color = "grey15"
  # ) +

  # colors
  #scale_color_manual(values = location_colors, guide = "legend", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = location_colors,
    breaks = legend_breaks,
    labels = legend_labels,
    guide = guide_legend(title = NULL, byrow = TRUE)
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Study median LOD" = 21), name = NULL) +

  # x-axis: log1p positions, labelled on the original concentration scale.
  # limits = c(0, 7) was a HARD limit: values above log1p 7 were dropped from
  # the data before plotting, not merely hidden (2 MBZP observations, which
  # reach 7.75). Panels now scale to their own analyte instead.
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = log1p_breaks,
    labels = label_log1p,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.02))
  ) +

  # scales = "free" (was "free_y"): with a shared x range, PFOA peaked at
  # log1p 3.25 and TCP at 4.48 while MBZP ran to 7.75, so the two low-range
  # analytes used well under half their panel width. Each analyte now gets a
  # range that fits it.
  facet_wrap(~ facet_label, scales = "free", nrow = 2) +

  labs(
    title = "Exposure Intervals by Location Across Child and Adult Populations",
        subtitle = "Points: observations (log1p scale). Open circle: study median LOD. Dot: median when available. Thick bar: IQR (Tau25–Tau75) when available. Thin bar: upper outer interval to Tau95.",
    x = "Concentration (original scale)",
    y = NULL,
    color = "Location"
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    # Title block
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),

    # Facet strips
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#F2F2F2", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),

    # Gridlines to aid reading across
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    # Axes
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    # Location labels restored. These were blanked in favour of hand-drawn
    # left-side geom_text labels -- but that layer is commented out above, so
    # the panel shipped with no y labels at all and location was recoverable
    # only by matching a point colour against a 27-entry legend containing
    # nine near-identical blues. facet scales are free_y, so each panel labels
    # exactly the locations it contains.
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey15"),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line.y = element_blank(),

    # Legend
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_markdown(size = 10),
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.key.height = unit(10, "mm"),
    legend.key.width  = unit(8, "mm"),

    # Panel spacing
    panel.spacing = unit(10, "pt")
  ) +
  guides(
    shape = guide_legend(
      order = 1,
      override.aes = list(size = 3, color = "#111111", fill = "white")
    ),
    color = guide_legend(
      order = 2,
      nrow = 4,
      byrow = TRUE,
      label.hjust = 0,
      label.theme = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 14, lineheight = 1.15),
      override.aes = list(size = 3.2, alpha = 1)
    ),
    size = "none"
  ) +

  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")  # allow left-side labels to breathe

print(all_plot)
dev.off()

save(all_plot,file = "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Plots/All_Country_Intervals.RData")
```
